The ground-floor south door occupies the +1.0 m bay with a full plain bay to its left and the corner pillar flush on its right. Visually this reads as a **plausible narrow medieval tower**, not as an obvious kit mis-assembly or SG-7 fail. Stone materials, door trim, and proportions are coherent with the square building and the procedural brick tower. SD-ENV-11 — Opening-aware exterior shell projection (ratified for W-031/W-035).

Rule: Openings are voids in the ivy-reachable exterior shell, consistent with W-028 mesh cull (no triangles in opening bands), SD-METRIC-2 (opening buckets ineligible), and SeedAnchors (wall brick only, not OPENING_REVEAL). AR-FIELD-3 naive projection p←p−Φ·∇̂Φ is correct on solid wall but MUST NOT be used when the result lies in an opening footprint — gradient then points through the void to the opposite/interior face (north door exterior → sunlit interior, east window → sill/lintel discontinuity).

Contract (SurfaceQuery.project_to_shell, TowerSdf path):
1. q := existing Newton projection (1 step TowerSdf / 2 MeshSdf).
2. opening_footprint(p) := true when (azimuth,y) falls inside any TowerSpec door/window span — reuse SD-METRIC-2 angular half-width asin(width/2/radius_outer) and height bands [0,door_height], [window_sill, window_sill+window_size]; same convention as coverage.gd _mask_out_opening and tower_builder _spans_*.
3. If opening_footprint(q) OR opening_footprint(p+jitter source): discard q. snap := nearest point on exterior cylinder r=radius_outer by clamping azimuth and/or y out of the opening footprint to the nearest jamb/sill/lintel edge (minimize distance to original p; tie-break: prefer height snap for horizontal window bands). Return snap.
4. Do NOT return interior/back-face points. Do NOT return SD-EDGE-15 fallback for in-footprint queries — adjacent jamb brick must supply local field.
5. grad_S_D_L unchanged structurally: jitter→project_to_shell→trilinear; NO separate gradient clamp/mask. Saturation fix is projection-only.
